root_cause.text: The `need_futex_hash_allocate_default()` function incorrectly required both `CLONE_THREAD` and `CLONE_VM` to trigger default futex hash allocation, so when processes share memory via `CLONE_VM` without `CLONE_THREAD` (e.g., non-thread `clone()` calls), the percpu `mm->futex_ref` counter was not properly allocated or accounted, leading to a use-after-free when the counter was later accessed after the underlying memory had been freed.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states that the check "depends on strict pthread semantics, abusing CLONE_THREAD" and that this "breaks the non-concurrency assumptions when doing the mm->futex_ref pcpu allocations, leading to bugs[0] when sharing the mm in other ways; ie: BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in futex_hash_put". The patch loosens the condition from requiring both `CLONE_THREAD` and `CLONE_VM` to simply requiring `CLONE_VM` (excluding `CLONE_VFORK`), which fixes the oversight.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix futex hash allocation to cover all clone siblings that share mm, excluding vfork.
intent_record.what: The function need_futex_hash_allocate_default changed from returning true only when both CLONE_THREAD and CLONE_VM are set, to returning true when CLONE_VM is set and CLONE_VFORK is not set; a comment explaining the intent was added.
intent_record.how: The change broadens the condition for allocating a default futex hash: previously only thread siblings (CLONE_THREAD|CLONE_VM) triggered allocation; now any sibling that shares the parent's mm (CLONE_VM) except vfork (CLONE_VFORK) will trigger allocation. This means forked processes that do not set CLONE_THREAD but share mm (if any) will now allocate a futex hash, while vfork will not.
